items: Diagnose Before Acting, Item 1: Pour a bucket of water directly into the toilet bowl and watch what happens to determine if you have a soft clog (water drains slowly) or hard clog (water doesn't move).
Diagnose Before Acting, Item 2: Push the plunger down once hard and watch the water in the bowl to confirm the drain is open before committing to plunging as your solution method.
Diagnose Before Acting, Item 3: Identify whether the clog is likely caused by excessive toilet paper, foreign objects, or sediment buildup based on who used the toilet and when the problem started.
Diagnose Before Acting, Item 4: Stop plunging immediately if the water doesn't move at all on your test push — you risk splashing sewage and wasting effort on a clog that needs mechanical clearing.

Use the Right Plunger, Item 1: Buy a toilet-specific plunger with a rubber flange (the T-shaped piece) extending below the cup — sink plungers with flat cups cannot seal against a toilet's curved bowl.

Use the Right Plunger, Item 2: Insert the plunger at a 45-degree angle with the flange going into the drain first, then press down firmly so the rubber cup fully covers the opening and creates a tight seal.
Use the Right Plunger, Item 3: Pump the plunger aggressively with 6 to 8 hard, full strokes — pump slowly on the push and forcefully on the pull to maximize pressure changes that dislodge the clog.

Use the Right Plunger, Item 4: Give plunging exactly three serious attempts with aggressive technique before stopping — if the clog hasn't moved after three rounds, switch to the toilet auger immediately.
Move to the Auger, Item 1: Purchase a toilet auger (closet auger) for $25–$40 at any hardware store — this is the same $35 tool plumbers use to justify their $200 service call.
Move to the Auger, Item 2: Insert the auger cable into the toilet drain at a shallow angle while rotating the handle clockwise to extend the cable without scraping or cracking the porcelain bowl.
Move to the Auger, Item 3: Continue cranking and feeding the cable until you feel resistance (the blockage), then rotate sharply to hook or break up the clog before slowly pulling the cable back out.

Move to the Auger, Item 4: Test the toilet with a trial flush after using the auger — if it drains normally the clog is cleared, but call a plumber if two auger attempts fail to restore normal drainage.
